subject: Midwave trajectory recon: prioritized scope, proposed capacity swap, and vendor gating
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Midwave trajectory recon: prioritized scope, proposed capacity swap, and vendor gating

Team —

Quick mid-quarter note ahead of QBR prep. Scanning the OKR board this morning, two things stand out:

1) Latency & throughput OKR (SERVE-3) is ~40% behind planned tokens served this quarter. The shortfall is primarily due to higher-than-expected tail latency on the regional serving pool and longer model warmups (KV cache churn).

2) A set of lower-priority experiments (infra PoCs + benchmarking for new kernel set) are currently occupying reserved GPU slots that we had planned to use for Dedicated customer ramp trials.

Proposal: a temporary capacity swap for 2 weeks — move one node from the infra PoC pool into the model-serving reserved pool, and pause the least urgent PoC runs. This should buy us runway to meet our throughput SLO and avoid a customer-impacting dilution in the QBR narrative.

Asks:
- Vanessa: can you own the operational swap and customer comms? We need confirmation by EOD Thu (2026-08-19).
- Markus: can infra run the 72-hour benchmark on the candidate node (baseline + optimized batching) starting Friday and share results Monday?
- Karthik: there is a vendor gating item with CloudWave (contract amendment for burst capacity). Can you start procurement outreach and confirm timeline?

Attached: QBR-deck-skeleton_v2.pptx (working), OKR-gap-matrix.csv (live numbers). I’ll cut a short slide for the exec readout once we lock the swap.

If we don’t do something quick the QBR narrative will show a regression in the customer-facing metrics — want to avoid that if feasible.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midwave trajectory recon: prioritized scope, proposed capacity swap, and vendor gating

SG — thanks for the concise callout. I agree we should avoid surface-level customer regressions in the QBR. Short replies / commitments:

- I can own the operational swap and customer-facing note. I’ll coordinate with CS to update the top-3 impacted accounts (Nora at Aurora, plus two others) and prepare a short FAQ for support.
- I want to flag a procurement gating item: CloudWave needs a short amendment to allow short-term burst nodes for Dedicated; that will require legal + procurement signoff. Karthik — can you take point?
- I’ll pause the two least valuable infra PoCs this week and reassign their jobs. I’ll also attach a customer-impact heatmap and a short rolling view that shows estimated delta (see attachment).

Deliverables / times:
- I’ll post a change window and runbook by 09:00 PT Thu (2026-08-19).
- Customer comms draft in the shared drive by EOD Thu.

One ask to infra (Markus): when you publish the benchmark results, include the expected tail-latency delta at p99 and the projected token-cost change so we have a crisp tradeoff for the exec slide.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachment: customer-impact-heatmap.png
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midwave trajectory recon: prioritized scope, proposed capacity swap, and vendor gating

Thanks — quick technical note and alternative option.

Option A (Sergio/Vanessa proposal): do the 2-week capacity swap. I can schedule the benchmark to run starting Fri; we’ll run baseline + optimized batching + KV-cache warmup trace. Expect a preliminary report by Mon morning.

Option B (optimize in-place): instead of swapping nodes, we throttle low-value PoC jobs more aggressively and push a conservative batching optimization across the regional pool. This gives us less friction (no contract amendment) but the risk is the savings may only be ~8–12% while swap looks like it would be ~18–25% improvement on tokens/sec based on earlier runs.

If Vanessa is confident we can pause the PoCs quickly, Option A buys time and clearer metrics for the QBR. Either way, we should run a short canary (100 qps steady-state) on the candidate node and validate p95/p99 latency under real traffic. I’ll tag the canary ticket SUP-4456 and link results to the QBR deck.

I’ll prepare the benchmark template and post a small runbook to the drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/infra-runbook-benchmarks

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midwave trajectory recon: prioritized scope, proposed capacity swap, and vendor gating

Agreed next steps (finalizing):

1) Execute capacity swap (Option A): Vanessa to own change window and customer notes. Run window: Sat 2026-08-21 02:00–04:00 PT; rollback plan included in the runbook. Vanessa will confirm the runbook by 09:00 Thu (per her note).

2) Canary + benchmark: Markus to run the 72-hour benchmark on the candidate node and the 100 qps canary starting Fri; post initial numbers in SUP-4456 and attach to the QBR deck. Expect preliminary numbers Mon morning.

3) Procurement gating: Karthik to contact Tim Han at CloudWave and run the amendment process. If legal/procurement needs a signed amendment, aim for fast-track (48 hours) or we will use a temporary internal waiver for the swap. Karthik — please confirm the timeline by EOD Thu.

4) QBR artifacts: I attached an updated QBR-deck-skeleton_v2.pptx with a placeholder slide for the swap decision. Once we have benchmark numbers and the runbook, I’ll finalize the exec slide.

Meeting: I’ll push a 20-min standup for Mon 2026-08-23 08:30 PT to review numbers and lock the narrative (invite: https://meet.google.com/lookup/qbr-sync-aug20).

Thanks all — appreciate the quick alignment. If anything blocks your deliverables, flag here and I’ll escalate.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
